Assume $p_n$ is a nonincreasing sequence of positive real numbers, and let $\varepsilon_n\in\{-1,1\}$ be such that the series $\sum_{n\geq 1}\varepsilon_n p_n$ converges. Then:
1. If $\sum_{n\geq 1} p_n$ diverges, then the upper limit of the arithmetic means of $\varepsilon_n$ is at least $0$ and the lower limit is at most $0$, that is,
$$\liminf_{n\to \infty}\frac{\varepsilon_1+\cdots+\varepsilon_n}{n}\leq 0\leq \limsup_{n\to \infty}\frac{\varepsilon_1+\cdots+\varepsilon_n}{n}.$$

    (hε : ∀ n, ε n = -1 ∨ ε n = 1)

          Filter.atTop) ∧
    Filter.Tendsto
